speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Notice of Motion.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It comes as we enter a post-SG60 phase in our nation building journey.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We begin this next phase at a time of profound global change.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For nearly eight decades, the world benefited from an international order that supported stability and economic cooperation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The system rested, in large part, on the leadership of the United States (US).

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It underwrote global security, championed open markets and helped form the institutions and rules that enabled shared prosperity across the world, including here in Asia.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That era has now come to an end.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The US is re-assessing, and in some areas undoing, key elements of the very system it once helped to build.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Trade rules that were once promoted are being set aside.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Global institutions are being bypassed and long-standing norms are becoming less reliable.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The cumulative effect is a weakening of the multilateral system.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Countries everywhere have less confidence that common rules will protect their interests.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a result, more states are resorting to unilateral action and some are becoming emboldened to do so.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, the guardrails that once managed disputes and tensions are eroding.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And so, the world is becoming more contested, more fragmented and ultimately more dangerous.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Against this backdrop, last year, there was widespread expectation that the US Liberation Day tariffs would trigger a sharp global slowdown.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many firms adjusted quickly – front-loading production and imports to get ahead of the tariff measures.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Subsequent trade deals, together with shifts in global supply chains, helped to reduce the actual impact of the tariffs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a result, growth in the major economies held up, supported in part by strong investment in artificial intelligence (AI)-related activities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In short, despite mounting stresses, the global economy proved more resilient than anticipated and the international system continued to function.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This year, however, we may not be so fortunate.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Events in just the first month of 2026 have already been of exceptional scale and consequence.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As pressures build and the margin for error narrows, the resilience of the global system will be tested far more severely.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There are also clear and growing signs of fragility in the global economy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Rising public debt in many major economies will strain financial stability and weigh on longer-term growth prospects.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, heightened risk-taking in financial markets has pushed up asset valuations, leaving them vulnerable to abrupt corrections.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Any such adjustment would dampen confidence and spill over into real economic activity.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These external developments have a direct bearing on us.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Strong external demand boosted key industry clusters, including electronics and biomedical manufacturing.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These gains generated spillovers across the broader economy.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite these uncertainties, we can move forward with confidence – confidence grounded in fundamentals.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the decades, we have systematically strengthened our economic foundations: deepening capabilities, investing in our people and reshaping our industries as technologies evolve.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have built a reputation as a reliable and trusted hub – stable, secure, and well-governed – qualities that businesses and investors have come to value highly, more so now than before, precisely because the world has become more fractured and uncertain.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All these give Singapore an important and tangible competitive advantage.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But past success alone will not carry us forward.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a profoundly changed world, standing still is not an option.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cannot wait for conditions to turn more favourable.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nor can we fall back on strategies designed for a previous era.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We therefore have a full agenda in this term of Government to refresh our strategies and strengthen our social compact.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Budget 2026 is the first step in this effort, to secure our future in a changed world.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It lays the groundwork for how we will navigate our next phase of development – together, as one people.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, we will: advance our refreshed economic strategy; harness artificial intelligence (AI) as a strategic advantage; build a resilient and skilled workforce; give families more support and greater assurance; protect our security and sustainability; and renew and strengthen our Singapore spirit.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I will touch on each of these in turn.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While our economy did well last year, some businesses continue to face cost pressures and operating challenges.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will provide short-term relief, as we press on with our restructuring and transformation efforts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Growth will be harder in this changed world.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must aim higher, move faster and be prepared to take calculated risks.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why the Government convened the Economic Strategy Review (ESR).

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The ESR committee shared their mid-term update last month and we will move decisively to act on their recommendations.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Growth must translate into good jobs and rising incomes for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: First, we must adapt and connect differently in a changed global environment.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some countries are turning inward, seeking to reduce their external dependence.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for Singapore that is not an option.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To prosper, we still need to be connected to the world – trading with others and integrating ourselves into global flows.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most major products still depend on a global division of labour, combining expertise and materials from many countries, and on access to global markets to achieve scale.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What has changed is globalisation as we knew it.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Economic flows are becoming more selective, partnerships more strategic and resilience now matters as much as efficiency.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, Singapore must adjust to these new patterns – staying open, but connecting in smarter, more diversified and more resilient ways.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we are forging new forms of cooperation with partners who share our commitment.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also step up engagement with fast-growing markets, including in Latin America, Africa and the Middle East.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will establish new embassies and strengthen our diplomatic and economic presence on the ground to take better advantage of emerging opportunities in these regions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Closer to home, we are working with our neighbours to deepen regional integration.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes cooperating on projects like the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone, and the Batam, Bintan and Karimun Free Trade Zones in Indonesia.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In short, we will redouble our efforts to diversify globally and to integrate regionally.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It must translate into real opportunities that our businesses can capture and seize.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It started in 1972 offering electrical installation services to oil refineries and petrochemical plants here in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But it did not confine itself to our domestic market.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over time, it built a leading presence in Southeast Asia delivering energy infrastructure services.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, it is venturing further afield and deepening its presence in the Middle East.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But doing business overseas is not easy, especially for smaller firms.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Companies face unfamiliar regulations, different business practices and intense local competition.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also enhance the Market Readiness Assistance grant to support companies not just to access new markets, but to deepen activities in existing overseas markets as well.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will give companies more flexibility to cater to their different financing needs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also provide more support for companies pursuing significant overseas ventures that require higher capital outlay.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Trade and Industry will share more about these changes at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we will build leadership in key growth clusters.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That means anchoring critical segments of global value chains here in Singapore, especially activities with high knowledge content and strong spillovers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our goal is not just to host such activities, but to shape how these industries develop and where they create value.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are already doing this in some areas like semiconductors.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A key frontier in semiconductors is Advanced Packaging.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Despite what the name suggests – Advanced Packaging – this is highly complex and technologically demanding.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Traditionally, faster chips have been built by packing more transistors onto a single chip.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But this is becoming more costly, and we are approaching physical limits.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a result, attention has shifted to Advanced Packaging, which integrates multiple chips into a single package, using highly precise manufacturing technologies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore began investing in Advanced Packaging research and development (R&D) more than two decades ago, well before it became a global priority.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are one reason why major semiconductor companies continue to invest heavily in Singapore, not just in manufacturing, but also in R&D, innovation and supply chain partnerships.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We see a similar pattern in other key industries like aerospace and biomedical sciences.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Technology is the critical enabler underpinning our strategy to build leadership in these clusters.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we must be realistic.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In absolute dollars, our public R&D spending will always be modest compared to the sums deployed by much larger economies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Instead, our investments must be disciplined, focused and strategic, directed at areas where Singapore has clear strengths and where our efforts can make a real difference.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is potential in emerging areas like decarbonisation solutions and quantum technology.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In quantum, for example, we made an early and deliberate bet.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In 2007, we established the Centre for Quantum Technologies at the National University of Singapore (NUS).

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Much of quantum research then was still theoretical.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we invested patiently in building foundational capabilities, believing that these would one day translate into transformative applications.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, quantum computing is moving rapidly from theory to reality, with far-reaching implications across many fields.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The major technology players are investing heavily in capabilities to build commercial-scale quantum computers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And Singapore is attracting some of the best.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Quantinuum, one of the world's leading quantum computer companies, has established operations here and will be hosting its latest quantum computer in Singapore, making us the first country outside America to host this system.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will give our researchers and companies, including a few home-grown startups, direct access to cutting-edge quantum compute and opportunities to work on meaningful projects.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also attracting top global talent and partnerships.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Nobel Laureate Prof John Martinis, a pioneer in superconducting systems, co-founded a quantum computing startup, which is collaborating with our researchers at the Agency for Science, Technology and Research (A*STAR) and NUS.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are developing novel components to advance the performance of quantum computers, using state-of-the-art semiconductor processes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They chose Singapore because of the unique combination of our strengths – in advanced manufacturing, semiconductors and frontier quantum research.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These examples show how we can build leadership in key growth areas, and shape where innovation and value creation take place.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In doing so, we strengthen Singapore's strategic resilience and relevance, while creating more jobs and better opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Enterprise funding is a key part of this ecosystem.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over many years, we have worked steadily to strengthen this area.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In venture and seed funding, we have made good progress.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Compared to a decade ago, it is now much easier for startups to access early-stage capital.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But many firms continue to face challenges at the growth stage.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As a result, many firms, especially in deep tech, find it harder to raise the larger and longer-term funding that is needed to scale.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will therefore do more to catalyse growth capital in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under the Startup SG Equity scheme, the Government provides initial capital to catalyse and crowd in private funding for promising startups.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond this, we will take a more systemic approach to strengthening our growth capital ecosystem.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will convene a new workgroup led by Minister Chee Hong Tat, working closely with the industry, to develop strategies to position Singapore as a leading centre for growth capital.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When enterprises are ready to list, we want them to see Singapore as their listing venue of choice.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As with the first tranche, this will be a co-investment between the Government and Temasek.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also continue to strengthen our broader equities market.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year, MAS launched the Equity Market Development Programme, to develop our fund management industry and increase investor participation in Singapore equities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MAS has allocated close to $4 billion to nine asset managers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These measures will enhance the depth and vibrancy of our public equities market and provide more pathways for enterprises to grow and scale from Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Deep and vibrant markets are one part of the equation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must also ensure a strong pipeline of high-quality companies that choose to build, grow and anchor themselves in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Economic Development Board has traditionally focused its investment promotion efforts on multi-national enterprises.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Going forward, it will step up efforts to attract high-growth companies with the potential to become future industry leaders.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By anchoring such companies early, we can build new engines of growth and capture greater value for our economy as these enterprises grow and expand from Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This comprehensive approach – from nurturing homegrown startups, to catalysing private capital and attracting promising global companies – will strengthen our enterprise ecosystem.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It will enable companies of all sizes and at every stage of growth, to access the capital and partnerships they need to succeed.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Importantly, this will create more opportunities for Singaporeans to secure good jobs and grow their careers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a changed world, a decisive factor for success will be how we harness new technologies – foremost amongst them, AI.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are reaching a stage where systems can write their own code and improve through iterative learning.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The potential is immense – to raise productivity, unlock new discoveries and transform lives in ways that we are only beginning to understand.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Societies worry about misinformation, bias and the ethical use of powerful technologies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These anxieties are real and we must confront them squarely.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we allow uncertainty to paralyse us, we will fall behind in a world that is moving rapidly ahead.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we must act with clarity and resolve.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: AI is a powerful tool, but it is still a tool.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It must serve our national interests and our people.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will define how AI is developed and used in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will set clear rules to ensure it is applied responsibly and safely.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we will ensure that its benefits are shared widely across society.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Harnessed well, AI will be a strategic advantage for Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It can help us overcome our structural constraints – our limited natural resources, rapidly ageing population and tight labour market.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To do this, we must invest deliberately and with discipline, not by simply following what others do, but by playing to Singapore's strengths.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our advantage does not lie in building the largest frontier models.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It lies in deploying AI effectively, responsibly and at speed.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore can be a trusted hub where companies and researchers come together to develop, test and deploy impactful AI solutions – and do so faster and more coherently than many larger countries.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These investments have created a growing number of good jobs for Singaporeans, in AI research, engineering and deployment.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But to fully realise AI's potential, we must go beyond individual pilots and isolated experiments.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, in advanced manufacturing, we aim to accelerate innovation and build best-in-class factories that can compete globally.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In connectivity and logistics, AI can help to automate airport and seaport operations, move goods more efficiently, and strengthen Singapore's position as a leading global hub.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Each AI Mission will be anchored in clear objectives and tangible outcomes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Delivering this will require us to work differently.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will review regulations and create sandboxes, so that companies can test AI innovations safely and responsibly.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Within the Government, we will better align our R&D, regulatory and investment promotion efforts so that agencies act in concert and pull in the same direction.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For AI to truly transform our economy, companies must also adopt it comprehensively.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But end-to-end transformation with AI is very demanding.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It requires organising data, rebuilding systems, redesigning processes and jobs, and retraining workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even the major global companies are grappling with this.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But those that succeed will gain a decisive competitive advantage.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A few leading Singapore companies like DBS and Grab are already moving decisively on AI transformation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Support will be tailored to each company, and will include enterprise transformation and workforce training.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As these companies succeed, they will set benchmarks for their industries and inspire others to follow.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond this, we will strengthen support for all enterprises, especially our SMEs, so they adopt AI and benefit from it in practical ways.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also strengthen our existing support schemes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Productivity Solutions Grant (PSG) already helps companies to adopt digital solutions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take HarriAnns, an F&B company known for its freshly made nonya kueh.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It began in the 1940s, started by Mdm Chia Nguk Eng, and later grew into a stall at Tiong Bahru Food Centre.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the 1980s, her son took over the business.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, the third generation runs the company, and it has expanded to eight cafes across Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To build a vibrant AI-enabled economy, it helps to have a focal point – one that brings together AI founders, practitioners, researchers and innovators, and catalyses more collaborations and interactions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have started a pilot initiative called Lorong AI.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will be a new cluster to catalyse ideas, forge collaborations and translate AI initiatives into practical solutions for businesses and public services.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Just as we support enterprises, we must do the same and more, for our workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I know this creates real anxiety for workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The pace of change can be unsettling, especially when livelihoods are at stake.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we will not allow technological change to come at the expense of our workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will press ahead with AI – because we must.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we will put in place strong support to help our workers adapt and progress – because we will take care of our own.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will stand with our workers throughout this transition.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: No one will have to navigate the changes alone.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will help Singaporeans acquire new skills, adapt to new roles, and use AI as a tool to be more productive and effective at work.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Where jobs are impacted, we will manage the transitions carefully, and work closely with the National Trades Union Congress (NTUC) and our unions to help workers move into new areas and opportunities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our commitment is clear: every Singaporean who is willing to adapt and learn will continue to secure a good job and make a good living here in Singapore.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To succeed in this new reality, we must prepare both our future workforce and those already working today.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Just as importantly, our IHLs will continue to emphasise strong foundations, so that students learn to use AI wisely, not as a shortcut, and are equipped with rigorous thinking and deep disciplinary skills.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the workplace, we will help workers use AI to take over routine tasks, so that they can focus their time and energy on higher-value activities – work that requires judgement, creativity and human insight, and that cannot be replaced by machines.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, accountants can use AI to automate large parts of data consolidation, preparation and book-keeping.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This allows them to move up the value chain, spending more time on client advisory, forensic work and complex analysis, where professional expertise and trust matter most.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To support workers through this transition, we will help them build practical AI capabilities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond these specific sectors, every Singaporean can take the initiative to learn and pick up AI-related skills.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, many AI chatbots, like ChatGPT or Gemini, are widely available and easy to use.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For many, they are just smarter versions of a search engine.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there is much more to AI than just doing a search.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With the right guidance and prompts, these tools can do a lot more – helping users analyse information, generate ideas nd solve problems.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Using AI well requires learning, practice and the right support.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: There is already a wide range of AI-related courses on the SkillsFuture website, from fully online options to part-time and full-time programmes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While most AI tools are free at the basic level, access to more advanced models requires a paid subscription.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will allow them to practise, experiment and apply what they have learnt.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Several Ministries – the Ministry of Digital Development and Information, the Ministry of Education (MOE), the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) and the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) – are involved in these cross-cutting efforts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And the Ministers will provide more details at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to move forward with confidence.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: By harnessing AI as a strategic advantage, we will shape our own future and secure our place in this changed world.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singaporeans, and especially our workers, are at the centre of everything we do.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ultimately, what matters is not just the policies we announce, but the outcomes they deliver in people's lives.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why we track results carefully and assess whether our efforts are making a real difference.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Earlier this week, MOF released an Occasional Paper on income growth, inequality and social mobility trends.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It shows that over the past decade, we have made good progress with broad-based wage increases and smaller income gaps.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Left entirely to market forces, they would not have occurred on their own.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, in many advanced economies, as growth slows, inequality becomes more entrenched.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why the Government has and will continue to lean against these trends, and strive to ensure that the fruits of growth are shared widely and fairly.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Every Singaporean, regardless of where they start in life, should have a fair chance to pursue their aspirations and realise their full potential.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, in this Budget, we will continue to strengthen support for lower-wage workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will better encourage and reward the firms that invest in their workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These measures build on the Progressive Wage Model (PWM), which we have developed together with NTUC and our tripartite partners.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The PWM goes beyond a simple flat minimum wage and instead links pay increases to skills, productivity and career progression – and it is delivering results.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also continue to strengthen training support for the PWM.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year, I announced additional support under the Workfare Skills Support for workers who take up long-form training courses.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will go further to enhance the basic tier of the scheme and increase the hourly allowance for workers who upgrade their skills.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also do more to support lifelong learning for all Singaporeans through SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When we first started SkillsFuture more than a decade ago, the training landscape looked very different.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At that time, our IHLs were still largely focussed on pre-employment training.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But we knew this was no longer sufficient.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That was why we set up SkillsFuture Singapore in 2016 under MOE to embed lifelong learning within our education system.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Working adults at all stages of their careers can access a wide range of high-quality training options across our IHLs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All our autonomous universities, polytechnics and Institutes of Technical Education (ITE) have internalised lifelong learning as part of their mission.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, NUS and the Nanyang Technological University (NTU), our two largest universities, have made lifelong learning an integral part of how they organise their teaching and learning.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They offer flexible pathways for alumni and adult learners to take modular courses, earn stackable credits and progressively build these into recognised qualifications.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year, more than 600,000 individuals took up training with SkillsFuture support, offered by IHLs and private training providers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While SkillsFuture Singapore under MOE focused on skills training, we also had Workforce Singapore under MOM to engage employers and help jobseekers find jobs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the years, we have worked to strengthen coordination between these two agencies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in an era of faster technological change and more frequent job transitions, stronger alignment is needed, and our systems must work more seamlessly together.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Hence, the ESR committee recommended that the Government review how we organise jobs and skills support for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For workers and jobseekers, that means support will be more seamless – from career planning, to skills acquisitions, and job matching and transitions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For employers, the support will be more integrated – covering workforce planning, job redesign, hiring and workforce development.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Education and the Minister for Manpower will share more at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is about continually strengthening our system of lifelong learning and career support, so Singaporeans can continue to adapt, grow and realise their full potential.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In a world where change is constant, we must remain a society that never stops learning and never stops striving to do better.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also strengthening support for specific segments of our workforce.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In 2024, we launched the SkillsFuture Level-Up Programme to help mid-career workers undergo a skills reboot.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The take-up has been encouraging: over 60,000 Singaporeans aged 40 and above have already benefitted from substantial training courses.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Mr Jeffrey Loh is one of the many adult learners who has benefited from the programme.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: After 18 years as an air steward, he was keen to reskill and pursue new opportunities aligned with his interests.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, he enrolled in a Digital Product Management course at the Singapore Institute of Technology.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Most of his course fees were offset by SkillsFuture subsidies and credits.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He also received the Mid-Career Training Allowance during the three-month course, which helped support his daily expenses while he trained.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, Jeffrey is doing well in a new role as a Duty Terminal Manager with Changi Airport Group.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to enhance the Level-Up programme.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also expand coverage to include more industry relevant courses.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will support our seniors so they can continue to contribute meaningfully.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes helping them plan ahead for their later-stage careers and supporting them in refreshing their skills.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also equip employers to design age-friendly jobs and multi-generational workplaces.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: MOM has convened a Tripartite Workgroup on Senior Employment to study these issues comprehensively.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Their recommendations will be released later this year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As we create better jobs and upskill Singaporeans, we must also remain open to global skills and talent.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Foreign professionals and workers strengthen our teams, transfer knowledge and enable companies to grow.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This in turn creates more and better opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we will continue to ensure that our foreign workforce complements a strong Singaporean core.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This maintains the quality of the EP holders, as local wages rise.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The qualifying salaries for older EP applicants will be raised in tandem.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For renewal applications, the changes will apply a year later in 2028, to give businesses more time to adjust.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Likewise, we will raise the qualifying salaries for S Pass holders.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For the financial services sector, this will be raised from $3,800 to $4,000.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Qualifying salaries for older S Pass applicants will be raised in tandem, with renewal applications affected one year later, from 2028.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For the Marine and Process sectors, levies for basic skilled workers will be raised by $100 and $150, respectively.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For the Manufacturing and Services sectors, we will simplify the current tiered levy structure.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The details are in the Annex to the Budget.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To give businesses time to adjust, these changes will take effect from 2028.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Manpower will share more at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The wide range of workforce measures I have outlined reflects Singapore's overall approach: to stay open to skills and expertise that strengthen our economy, while ensuring that Singaporeans remain firmly at the centre of our workforce and our policies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will help Singaporeans adapt to change with confidence, move across career transitions with assurance, and build meaningful and fulfilling careers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through Forward Singapore, we have made significant moves in recent years to support Singaporeans and their families – from parents, to seniors, caregivers and persons with disabilities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have also ramped up the supply of HDB flats to ensure that public housing remains accessible and affordable for couples and families.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, we will make further moves to give families more support and greater assurance.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We want to create the right conditions, so they feel confident and ready to start a family.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The decision to get married and have children is deeply personal.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for those who wish to take the step, the Government will do more to support them along the way.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One of the biggest concerns for young couples is the cost of raising a family.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over successive Budgets, we have strengthened support to help parents manage these expenses.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For example, we introduced the Large Families Scheme to support families who have, or aspire to have, three or more children.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For every third or subsequent child, the scheme will provide up to $16,000 in additional benefits.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to keep preschool and student care affordable, to support the critical early years of a child's development.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the years, we have reduced preschool fee caps and increased subsidies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, childcare fees for dual-income families are comparable to primary school and after-school student care fees.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Lower- and middle-income families also receive means-tested subsidies, which further reduce out-of-pocket expenses.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From the start of next year, we will extend means-tested preschool subsidies to more families, by raising the monthly household income threshold to $15,000.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Eligible parents, including those who previously qualified, can also receive more in infant care and childcare subsidies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond these enhancements, we are undertaking a holistic review of the student care sector to study how to better meet the caregiving needs of families with primary school-aged children.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to help lower-income families, especially those with young children, move towards greater stability, self-reliance and social mobility.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We take a family-centric approach to support such families.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Under ComLink+, each family is paired with a dedicated family coach, who works with them to develop personalised action plans and to coordinate support.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To recognise and reinforce the families' own efforts, we introduced Progress Packages.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These are more than financial assistance; they are a form of social contract where family coaches work with the families to set clear goals, like securing a stable job, saving towards a home, or ensuring their children enrol in and attend preschool regularly.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: When these milestones are achieved, the families receive additional payouts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take Mdm Hurul and Mr Hafiz for example.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They had taken important steps on their own to stabilise their finances.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: What they needed was sustained guidance and support to keep moving forward.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With support from their family coach, and through their own hard work, they have made good progress over the past year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through the Progress Packages, their financial circumstances have improved, and they are now closer to securing their own 4-room HDB flat.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: ComLink+ is built around close and sustained support for families.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It relies on dedicated family coaches, case workers from Family Service Centres and volunteer befrienders who work directly with families to help them make steady progress.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over time, we have strengthened our capabilities on the ground and we are now ready to enhance the ComLink+ Progress Packages.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, we will enhance the additional payouts that families receive when they make concrete progress in their goals of maintaining stable employment and good preschool attendance for their children.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, we will provide more of these payouts in cash, while continuing to set aside monies in their CPF accounts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help families meet immediate needs, while also building their longer-term financial security.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And we hope this will provide them with the necessary support to stabilise their finances and secure a better life for themselves and their children.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Minister for Social and Family Development will provide more details at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also do more for persons with disabilities, as well as their families and caregivers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Minister of State Goh Pei Ming is leading a task force to review how we can provide more meaningful support at different life stages for persons with disabilities and their families.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This includes expanding capacity in community-based facilities, keeping services affordable, and supporting graduates of special education schools to secure meaningful employment and live well in the community.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We look forward to the recommendations of the task force.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Strengthening support for persons with disabilities is a key priority for the Government and a shared responsibility for all of us.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, the Government stands ready to set aside additional resources to advance these efforts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: As our population ages, we will also provide more support for our seniors so they can age with dignity, security and peace of mind.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We recently enhanced CareShield Life to provide higher payouts, giving seniors greater assurance against long-term care costs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: With longer lifespans, retirement adequacy is another major concern for many Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our aim is clear: Singaporeans who work and contribute to CPF consistently should be able to meet their basic retirement needs with confidence.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the years, we have enhanced the CPF system to achieve this.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We introduced Silver Support to uplift seniors with less means and the Majulah Package to give additional assurance to our "Young Seniors" as they approach retirement.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In this Budget, we will take further steps to strengthen retirement support.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Those with lower balances will receive larger top-ups, so that support is targeted at where it is most needed.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will help older workers build up their retirement savings in their later working years.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will also continue to provide the CPF Transition Offset to employers, covering half of the increase in employer contributions for 2027.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, we will offer more investment options for CPF members who wish to grow their savings further.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, the CPF system provides stable, risk-free interest rates to help Singaporeans build up their retirement nest egg.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some CPF members, especially those with a longer runway to retirement, are prepared to take more risk to generate potentially higher returns.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But experience shows that most people do not do well picking and trading individual stocks.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is very hard to beat the market consistently.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For retail investors, a more sensible approach is broad and diversified exposure through low-cost funds.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Because some may invest when markets are high, and retire during a downturn, precisely when they need their savings.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why the CPF Advisory Panel earlier recommended introducing a Lifetime Retirement Investment Scheme.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is essentially a life-cycle investment approach, with a predefined glide path to retirement.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In other words, members take on more risk, with greater exposure to equities, when they are younger; and their investments are automatically rebalanced towards safer assets as they approach retirement.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Later this year, CPF Board will engage the industry and invite expressions of interest from potential providers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will also be prepared, in-principle, to provide some time-limited support to kick-start the scheme.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: CPF members can choose whether to opt in.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, we will strengthen efforts to help members understand whether this option is suitable for them – in particular, for members who are younger and have a long runway to retirement, and who can better ride out short-term market fluctuations.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I have set out the broad framework today.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But there are still many details to work out, and MOM and CPF Board will share more when ready.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will continue to do whatever is necessary to help Singaporeans manage cost pressures for as long as it is needed.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Although inflation has eased in recent years, we know that many Singaporeans still face anxieties and pressures.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will continue to provide additional support this year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Second, there will be additional U-Save rebates to help households with their utilities expenses.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Third, I will provide another $500 in Community Development Council (CDC) Vouchers   for all Singaporean households in January 2027.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Similar to previous rounds of CDC Vouchers, half can be used at participating supermarkets, while the other half can be used at participating heartland merchants and hawkers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will keep working at this, steadily and responsibly, so that Singapore remains an inclusive and united society and a place that we are all proud to call home.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Next, let me touch on security challenges as well as our longer-term sustainability concerns.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The world has never been free of conflict.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But in recent years, it has become more dangerous.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In 2024 alone, there were 61 state-based armed conflicts worldwide, the highest number recorded since the Second World War.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The conflicts are not confined to distant regions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Closer to home, we witnessed one of the most serious armed clashes involving Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) member states in years.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A long-standing border dispute between Cambodia and Thailand escalated into an open military confrontation – drones, rocket launchers and even fighter jets were deployed.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Civilians were wounded, displaced and lives were lost.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They reflect a shrinking space for negotiation, a greater willingness to use force, and a higher risk of miscalculation, with consequences that can easily spill across borders.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: History has taught us a hard lesson: no one will come to our rescue if Singapore faces a crisis.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We alone are responsible for our defence and survival.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is why we must stay vigilant and be prepared for a wider range of security challenges.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since Independence, we have invested steadily to safeguard Singapore's peace and stability.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That has allowed us to adopt new technologies, and build credible and strong capabilities in both the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) and the Home Team.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The recent conflicts we see around us have also underscored how the nature of warfare is changing.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unmanned aerial systems are now a common feature of modern conflict.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They are used not only for surveillance, but also for precision strikes, electronic warfare and coordinated operations.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Drones are cheaper, more accessible and increasingly sophisticated, allowing even smaller actors to project force in new ways.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will invest decisively in capabilities that are essential to Singapore's defence.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: And that includes strengthening our ability to deploy, counter and operate alongside unmanned systems across all domains.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They range from scams targeting individuals, to highly sophisticated attacks on critical information systems.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have faced attacks from malicious cyber actors, including hostile information campaigns and deliberate attempts to undermine our national security.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Over the years, we have strengthened our defences.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We established the Cyber Security Agency; built expertise within the Home Team Science and Technology Agency; and stood up the Digital and Intelligence Service in the SAF.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These efforts have enabled us to detect, disrupt and fend off many attacks.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But the threat landscape continues to evolve, with attacks becoming more frequent, more coordinated and more sophisticated.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will therefore continue to strengthen our cybersecurity posture by deepening capabilities, improving coordination across agencies and better safeguarding our most critical systems.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is also no longer sufficient to defend government systems alone.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many private sector companies play a critical role in delivering essential services and their systems are likewise vulnerable.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The attackers often exploit smaller or less-protected companies as weak links to gain access to larger systems, and cause widespread disruption.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Yet many companies lack the resources or expertise to deal with these advanced cyber threats.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we will therefore deepen partnerships with industry, especially owners of critical information systems to improve our preparedness and strengthen our collective cyber defence.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: All this underscores the importance of sustained investments in our security.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Importantly, our security effort goes beyond the Ministry of Defence alone.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It also includes investments in the security of our critical infrastructure and in the Home Team.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Taken together, we expect overall security-related expenditures to rise in the coming years to keep Singapore safe and secure in a far more complex threat environment.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond immediate security threats, we must also confront a longer-term challenge to Singapore and that is the growing impact of climate change.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are already feeling its effects: higher temperatures, heavier rainfall, and more frequent extreme weather events.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Unfortunately, global momentum on climate action has slowed.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the 30th Conference of the Parties in Brazil last November, countries were unable to agree on concrete decarbonisation roadmaps.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At around the same time, the International Maritime Organization delayed adoption of its Net Zero framework, as member states could not reach consensus.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Some governments are scaling back their climate ambitions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But for Singapore, retreating from action is not an option.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to do our part, not only to address climate risks, but also to secure our longer-term resilience and competitiveness.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: A key pillar of our climate strategy is the carbon tax.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It sends a clear price signal to encourage emissions reduction.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Firms are investing more in low-carbon solutions, and improving energy efficiency.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had earlier announced our carbon tax trajectory for this decade.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For HDB households, the additional U-Save rebates that I highlighted earlier will help to cushion the impact of the carbon tax.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For businesses, we will extend the Energy Efficiency Grant and support for green loans under the Enterprise Financing Scheme.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These will help firms invest in energy-efficient and sustainable solutions.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While Singapore will continue to contribute responsibly to climate action, we recognise that our actions alone cannot determine global outcomes.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will therefore calibrate our moves cautiously, doing our part to reduce emissions as a responsible global citizen, while taking into account what other countries are doing, in order not to put ourselves at a competitive disadvantage.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, beyond 2027, we are assessing Singapore's carbon tax trajectory carefully, in light of international developments.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore already has the highest carbon tax rate in the whole of Asia.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Looking further ahead, our path to net zero will depend heavily on technological breakthroughs and sustained international cooperation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Without these, it will be increasingly difficult for a small, resource-constrained country like Singapore to move further on our own.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The progress of our transition to net zero may therefore be uneven.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But our efforts will be credible, forward-looking and aligned with global realities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even amidst these uncertainties, we continue to make concrete progress.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will therefore raise the target to three gigawatt-peak by 2030.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond that, we will continue to maximise solar deployment across all viable surfaces and progressively set more ambitious targets further into the future.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also advancing plans to import low-carbon electricity from the region.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: While not all will materialise, those that do will help to reduce our carbon footprint and strengthen our energy resilience.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In transport, we remain committed to achieving 100% cleaner vehicles by 2040.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Incentives are in place to encourage early adoption of electric vehicles and charging infrastructure is being expanded nation-wide.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are also greening our aviation and maritime sectors.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In shipping, we are partnering industry to develop a low-carbon ammonia bunkering solution on Jurong Island.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If successful, Singapore will be among the first countries in the world to supply ammonia commercially as a fuel for international shipping.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will face these challenges squarely and overcome them one by one.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is how we will move forward, steadily and decisively, to build a safer and more sustainable home for generations to come.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singapore's greatest strength lies not just in our policies and plans, but in the spirit of our people.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Time and again, we have defied the odds – not by chance, but by standing together as one people, especially in our most testing moments, whether it be Separation or financial crises or the current geopolitical uncertainties.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Around the world, we see growing polarisation and a tendency for groups to turn on each other.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Many societies are becoming more divided and more ungovernable.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, in this Budget, we will continue to invest in renewing and strengthening the bonds that bind us.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But they were not formed overnight, nor by chance.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They were built patiently and deliberately, generation after generation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our arts and heritage play a vital role in this journey.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They help us understand where we came from, express who we are today, and imagine who we can become as a people.
