speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Multiculturalism is a defining part of our identity.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We cherish and embrace our distinct cultural traditions and heritage, even as we continue to build common ground and a shared identity that unites us as Singaporeans.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our cultural and heritage institutions embody this approach – celebrating the richness of each community, while expressing our distinctive Singaporean identity.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will open the revamped Malay Heritage Centre later this year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will work with the Singapore Chinese Cultural Centre to expand its reach and engagement.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Indian Heritage Centre just marked its 10th anniversary, and we will provide further support to enhance its outreach and programming.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Sport is another powerful force that brings Singaporeans together.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Through sport, we learn resilience, teamwork and the determination to press on even when the odds are stacked against us.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will continue to roll out the Sports Facilities Master Plan, so that Singaporeans can more easily access affordable and quality sports facilities.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the coming years, we will open the new Punggol Regional Sport Centre, the Toa Payoh Integrated Development, sport facilities in Farrer Park and Tengah, as well as revamped sport centres in Hougang and Queenstown.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also expand the Dual-Use Scheme, so that Singaporeans can conveniently access sports facilities in schools.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will complement these facilities with more sports programming, bringing Singaporeans of all ages and abilities together through shared participation.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the foundation of our shared bonds, we must continue to nurture a strong sense of solidarity.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We see this in giving, volunteering and everyday acts of kindness.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These actions break down barriers, draw us closer, and remind us that we are all in this together.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They form the foundation of a "we first" society.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government will do our part to encourage and support this.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Beyond financial contributions, many Singaporeans give something equally valuable – their time and skills through volunteering.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This spirit of giving can be strengthened when companies make it easier for their employees to serve the community.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is why the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY) and the National Council of Social Service have been working closely with professional groups and industry bodies to encourage businesses to integrate giving, volunteering and socially responsible practices into their operations.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Singaporeans also contribute by starting ground-up initiatives to meet community needs.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Government supports such efforts through the "Our Singapore Fund".

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Since its introduction in 2016, the fund has supported over 800 ground-up projects, from community-building and sports, to municipal and digital readiness initiatives.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One example is "Little Hands, Big Hearts SG".

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is an initiative by Kaizen and Kay, aged 7 and 9, together with their parents, to involve others in monthly community service projects.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Their first project focussed on fire safety awareness.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They designed a poster and worked with the Nee Soon Town Council to display it at Housing and Development Board (HDB) lift lobbies.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They also brought other children and their families to visit Yishun Fire Station, where they presented care packs and handmade gifts to the officers on duty.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They have more projects in the pipeline: from a beach clean-up and support for seniors, to donating school supplies to children and writing appreciation cards to our migrant workers.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a wonderful example that shows anyone, no matter how young, can step up to make a difference.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Last year alone, the Our Singapore Fund received more than 250 applications.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will also continue to partner our youths and open up more avenues for them to shape Singapore's future.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Youth Panels have enabled young Singaporeans to work with the Government on issues that matter to them.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In the first round, 120 youths contributed across four Panels.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will launch the next round of Youth Panels later this year, enabling more young people to step forward and make a difference.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The Acting Minister for Culture, Community and Youth will share more details on these initiatives at the Committee of Supply.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This conviction is captured in our Pledge, which begins with "we", and affirms that we are "one united people".

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That sense of togetherness has carried us through uncertainty and brought us this far.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: If we continue to invest in one another – strengthening our bonds, looking out for those around us and putting the common good first, we can face the future with confidence and build a Singapore that endures and thrives.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now, let me touch on our fiscal position.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our prudent fiscal approach remains one of Singapore's core strengths.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We manage our public finances with discipline and care, ensuring that revenues are sufficient to meet expenditures, and that every dollar is used responsibly, for the benefit of both present and future generations.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The changes we made in the last term of Government have put Singapore on a healthy and sound fiscal footing.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We have a tax and transfer system that is fair, progressive and anchored on shared responsibility.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That gives us the capability and confidence to move forward.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Currently, car buyers are taxed through the Additional Registration Fee.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: To encourage timely renewal of the vehicle population so that it is safer and less pollutive, we provide a Preferential Additional Registration Fee (PARF) rebate for cars deregistered by their 10th year.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is sized as a percentage of the Additional Registration Fee paid.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Electric vehicles (EVs) are less pollutive than conventional petrol cars.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will apply to all cars registered with Certificates of Entitlement obtained from the next bidding exercise.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: The details of these tax changes are in the Annex.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For Financial Year (FY) 2025, we expect higher revenues.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is partly due to the better-than-expected economic performance, which I shared earlier.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Another key driver is the increase in our Corporate Income Tax collections.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: In FY2024, Corporate Income Tax contributed 4% of GDP – significantly higher than in past years.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I talked about this in our last Budget.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Based on the latest estimates, we expect Corporate Income Tax collections to increase further in FY2025.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We also saw higher asset-related revenue collections such as Vehicle Quota Premiums and Stamp Duty, driven by strong demand for private vehicles and properties.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Therefore, I expect to end FY2025 with a surplus of $15.1 billion, or 1.9% of GDP.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: For FY2026, I expect a smaller surplus of $8.5 billion, or 1% of GDP.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Our approach remains to keep the budget balanced over time, and across the ups and downs of the economic cycle.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Looking beyond this Budget, our public finances remain sound and resilient.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: On the revenue side, we will proceed with the implementation of the Top-up Tax under Pillar Two of Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS).

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This will raise the effective tax rate for large multinational enterprises operating in Singapore to 15%.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: So, we expect higher corporate tax collections from FY2027 onwards.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At the same time, our spending needs will grow across multiple fronts.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We will need to invest more in expanding our overseas partnerships, and in building up deeper capabilities to keep Singapore safe and prepared for emerging threats.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Even with the BEPS initiative, many other countries are rolling out generous incentives to re-shore and on-shore major investments.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That is the reality of today's competitive landscape.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We had anticipated higher spending for healthcare and provided for it through the GST rate increase.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: But healthcare is not the only social need we must address.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We therefore expect both revenues and expenditures to continue rising.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This puts Singapore in a very different position from many other countries, where governments are constrained by debt and deficit pressures, and forced into difficult trade-offs over what to cut.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We are therefore able to invest meaningfully and responsibly in policies and programmes that benefit all Singaporeans – now and in the years ahead.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: I recently visited an exhibition at the National Gallery organised by the Founders' Memorial.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It takes us back to Singapore in the 1950s to the 1970s, and traces how our pioneers forged a shared identity amid diversity and uncertainty.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: One display revisits the Aneka Ragam Rakyat, or the People's Cultural Concerts, organised by the then Ministry of Culture shortly after we attained self-government.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At one of these concerts, Mr Lee Kuan Yew addressed the crowd and described Singaporeans as "not mere spectators", but "active participants" in building a nation that belonged to all.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Indeed, Singapore has come so far only because generations of Singaporeans stepped forward.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They took responsibility, contributed what they could and did their part to shape our collective future.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That same spirit is alive today, especially amongst our youths.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Take for example Ayuni Nur Izyanti Md Zuraimi.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Ayuni discovered her passion for volunteering at 15.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together with four friends, she started a non-profit called You(th) Can Do It .

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It connects youths with volunteer opportunities across different organisations via Telegram.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now 19 and studying Medical Biotechnology at Temasek Polytechnic, she continues to volunteer regularly with her friends, tutoring primary school students from disadvantaged families, and cleaning the homes of senior citizens.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: From a young age, Shantini helped care for her brother who has cerebral palsy and relies on a motorised wheelchair.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: That experience instilled in her a deep commitment to serve others.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: At just 11, she began volunteering at the Sree Narayana Mission Nursing Home.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, at 23 and studying nursing at NUS, she leads the operations for Project Caring Hearts, a volunteer initiative that supports palliative patients through befriending programmes and community outreach.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: He first became active in community service while studying Electrical Engineering at ITE College West, volunteering with the Heartware Network.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Two years ago, he joined a non-profit group as a volunteer to teach migrant workers digital skills.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Now 19 and a Computer Engineering student at Singapore Polytechnic, he remains deeply committed to this cause, driven by his belief that migrant workers, who have contributed so much to Singapore's development, also deserve opportunities to upskill and progress.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: These stories differ in form, but they are united in spirit.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: They remind us that nation-building has never been the work of a few, or of one generation alone.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is the cumulative effort of ordinary Singaporeans who choose, in their own ways, to step forward and make a difference.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Today, this sense of shared responsibility matters more than ever.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: We must be active participants, looking out for one another, strengthening our social bonds, and contributing to a Singapore that belongs to all of us.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: This is the conviction that underpins Budget 2026.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: It is a Budget to support Singaporeans today, prepare our society for tomorrow and enable us to navigate this changed world with confidence.

speaker: The Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
text: Together we will secure a stronger, fairer and brighter future for all.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Debate to be resumed on what day, Prime Minister?
